rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejection of earlier messengers repeated the Quraysh pattern: messengers came from God, and at least some people in every generation called them sorcerers or madmen.
rows.anchor: ولو بعضهم برضا الباقين : { ساحر أو مجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusations arise because messengers oppose customs that people follow from desire; ‘or’ may distinguish different speakers’ accusations or express doubt, since sorcery implies cleverness while madness implies its opposite.
rows.anchor: سواء كانت ( أو ) للتفصيل بأن بعضهم قال واحدا وبعضهم قال آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether generations conspired to repeat the charge; they did not meet, but shared the trait of rebellious excess.
rows.anchor: لأن الأولين ما اجتمعوا مع الآخرين : { بل هم } اجتمعوا في وصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebellious are proud, excessive in unbelief, wrongdoing, and disobedience; the pronoun suggests transgression is ingrained in them, and God brings them to ruin through complete power and knowledge.
rows.anchor: عالون في الكفر مسرفون في الظلم والمعاصي مجاوزون للمقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After delivering the warning, the Prophet is told to turn away from further disputation and harsh confrontation; he is not blameworthy for their refusal.
rows.anchor: كلف نفسك الإعراض عن الإبلاغ في إبلاغهم بالمجادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should continue reminding gently because admonition benefits believers, who need repeated warnings to overcome desire and forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: أي بالرفق واللين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are those God has destined to be deeply rooted in faith; repeated reminders overcome their competing interests and appetites.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من إكثار التذكير ليلغلب ما عندهم من نوازع الحظوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish God’s universal mercy, inviting hope in His gifts and warning that He may end further favor through punishment; it does so by recounting creation’s wonders and blessings.
rows.anchor: فمقصودها بالذات إثبات الاتصاف بعموم الرحمة ترغيبا في إنعامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title ‘Bride of the Qur’an’ evokes its gathering of adornments, garments, jewels, crowns, blessings, beauty, and perfection.
rows.anchor: لأنها الحاوية لما فيه من حلى وحلل ، وجواهر وكلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God’s perfection as shown in creation, universal mercy in wondrous works and signs, and special mercy to the obedient through worship.
rows.anchor: الذي ظهر عموم رحمته بما بهر من بدائع مصنوعاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding surah’s emphasis on sovereignty and power, this surah counts blessings in both worlds; universal mercy completes kingship, and its opening name signals that theme.
rows.anchor: قصر هذه السورة على تعداد نعمه على خلقه في الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching the Qur’an is the greatest blessing: it is written and recited, gathers good, and distinguishes confusion; making this divine attribute accessible shows God can teach whom He wills.
rows.anchor: المرئي المشهود بالكتابة والمتلو المسموع الجامع لكل خير

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Burjān describes the name al-Raḥmān as the manifest aspect of the name Allah and the hidden aspect of the name al-Rabb; the three names disclose and veil the divine essence to creatures.
rows.anchor: قال ابن برجان : وهو ظاهر اسمه الله , وباطن اسمه الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars include celestial bodies and low-growing plants, while trees are rooted plants; both ‘prostrate’ by submitting to their appointed courses and yielding their benefits.
rows.anchor: أي وجميع الكواكب السماوية وكل نبت ارتفع من الأرض ولا ساق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The submission of sun, moon, stars, and trees points to the Creator’s unity and chosen action, refuting natural forces as independent causes.
rows.anchor: مما يدل على وحدانية الصانع وفعله بالاختيار , ونفي الطبائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s raising of the sky identifies Him as its effective cause; its ordered balance of seasons and measured precipitation manifests justice and sustains the earth.
rows.anchor: ودلنا على أنه شرع لنا مثل ذلك العدل لتقوم أحوالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance means justice that orders both cosmic realms; the Qur’an is a balance for knowledge and the scale a balance for sensible things.
rows.anchor: العدل الذي بدر به الخافقين من الموازنة وهي المعادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on transgressing the balance covers measured commodities as well as knowledge and action, and correspondence between outward and inward life, word and deed.
rows.anchor: الأشياء الموزونة من الموزونات المعروفة والعلم والعمل المقدر أحدهما بالآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must make all their actions conform to justice and must not diminish any instrument of justice, including measure, weight, judgment, or quantity; repeated mention stresses the command’s gravity.
rows.anchor: من الذرع والوزن والعدل والكيل ونحو - نوعا من أنواع الخسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah establishes resurrection as the disclosure of truth and defeat of falsehood, displaying comprehensive knowledge, complete power, and justice that separates the faithful from sinners; its title states this plainly.
rows.anchor: تنزيه الخالق ببعث الخلائق لإحقاق الحق وإزهاق الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala praises God’s perfection and justice, universal generosity, and special favor for those who keep His limits.
rows.anchor: الذي عم جوده بالعدل كبرا ومجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah is the certain Hour, where all matters appear in their realities and are judged justly; the name can mean both what is made true and what makes truth prevail over every opponent.
rows.anchor: فهي ثابتة في نفسها , ومن إحضار الأمور فيها بحقائقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question ‘What is the Reality?’ is an exclamation of magnification; grammatically the interrogative is the subject, al-Ḥāqqah its predicate, and repetition links it to the first statement while intensifying awe.
rows.anchor: وأكثر ما يكون ذلك إذا أريد معنى التعظيم والتهويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What has made you know’ refers to past knowledge and leaves the imagination open; no one can comprehend the Reality’s full nature before seeing it.
rows.anchor: أي إنها بحيث لا يعلم كنهها أحد ولا يدركها ولا يبلغها درايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding Sūrat Nūn warned against equating wrongdoers with the righteous and described judgment; the Day of Gathering is the Qur’an’s decisive reminder, and Jonah’s story demonstrates God’s power to bring it about.
rows.anchor: وقصة صاحب الحوت عليه السلام أدل دليل على القدرة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings began as nothing, then God moved them through reproductive stages; reflecting on this should expose their frailty and the folly of rejecting resurrection and divine favor.
rows.anchor: قد كان لا شيء فلا نطفة ولا علقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun ‘human’ generalizes to Adam and all his descendants, while the account then specifies the descendants’ creation from a small amount of male and female fluid.
rows.anchor: وأظهر ولم يضمر لأن الثاني خاص والأول عام لآدم عليه الصلاة والسلام وجميع ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nuṭfah is a small quantity of fluid in a container and the material carrying generative power; the author attributes different physical contributions to male and female fluids and says resemblance follows whichever fluid prevails.
rows.anchor: وما كان من عصب وعظم فمن نظفة الرجل , وما كان من دم ولحم وشعر فمن ماء المرأة

rows.speaker: يماني
rows.claim: Yamānī explains amshāj as any two colors mixed together.
rows.anchor: وقال يمان : كل لونين اختلطا فهو أمشاج

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains amshāj as the successive stages of creation, beginning with the drop and continuing afterward.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : هي أطوار الخلق من النطفة وما بعدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author describes fertilization and embryonic development as fluid mixing, clot, lump, differentiation into organs, and growth of the limbs and internal organs, all formed by God.
rows.anchor: فإذا اشتد ذلك الامتزاج وقوي وتمتن حتى استعد لأن يقسم فيه الأعضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit and body contend: the spirit is perfected while the body bears appetites and low impulses, so God strengthens the spirit through revealed law and prophetic teaching.
rows.anchor: قوى سبحانه الروح بالشرع الداعي إلى معالي الأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We test him’ means God subjects the person to commands, prohibitions, and exhortation as a test in human terms, though God already knows; this establishes proof and makes accountability intelligible to people.
rows.anchor: ونحن أعلم به منه , ولكنا فعلنا ذلك لنقيم عليه الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing and sight enable a person to perceive signs and arguments; hearing comes first because it serves address and audible signs are clearer than visible ones.
rows.anchor: وقدم السمع لأنه أنفع في المخاطبات

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the natural report ends here, after which acquired testing begins.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع وإلى هنا انتهى الخبر الفطري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit is created after the body is prepared; intellect and five outward senses let people register sensations, avoid harm, seek benefit, and become capable of moral responsibility.
rows.anchor: ثم أفاض سبحانه على الجملة العقل , وجعل السمع والبصر اللتين له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author outlines inward faculties: common sense receives perceptions, imagination stores images, estimation perceives particular meanings, memory stores them, and a combining faculty searches and rearranges them before intellectual knowledge.
rows.anchor: تسمى الحافظة باعتبار , والذاكرة باعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward faculties culminate in acquired intellect, the soul’s active presence of intelligibles and goal of its pursuit; theoretical reason serves practical reason and related faculties.
rows.anchor: وهذا العقل هو غاية السلوك الطلبي للإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides by making the clear path known through revealed books, messengers, signs within and beyond the self, and insight that distinguishes truth from falsehood and divine speech from human speech.
rows.anchor: بما أنزل من الكتب وأرسلنا من الرسل ونصبنا من الدلائل في الأنفس والآفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two human outcomes are thankfulness and ingratitude: shākir is an unmarked active participle because no one can fully thank every blessing, while kafūr is intensive because people can become deeply ungrateful, even by denying one favor.
rows.anchor: معرفا له أنه لا يأخذه إلا بالتوغل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thankfulness is named first as the human norm and because mercy precedes anger; ingratitude includes turning away, denial, worship of others, and stubbornness.
rows.anchor: وبدأ بالشكر لأنه الأصل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says every child is born upon the fiṭrah, after which parents make the child Jewish, Christian, or Magian; the author cites versions transmitted from Abū Hurayrah, Ibn ʿAbbās, Jābir, and al-Aswad ibn Surayʿ.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( كل مولود يولد على الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Sūrat al-Infiṭār stressed judgment and the recording of deeds, the surah warns against fraud in measures and gathers all who share that vice into its threat.
rows.anchor: وكان أعظم ما يدور بين العباد المقادير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl means immense, abiding ruin in every state of worldly and afterlife existence; mutaffifīn are those who reduce measure or weight and withhold people’s rights.
rows.anchor: هلاك ثابت عظيم في كل حال من أحوال الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects petty fraud with bad character and love of the world: habitual cheats come close to a full measure or fair weight but deliberately stop short.
rows.anchor: وهم من يقاربون ملء الكيل وعدل الوزن ولا يملؤون ولا يعدلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word taṭfīf may derive from ṭaff, the edge or projecting rim, and suggest removing what rises above a measure’s top.
rows.anchor: من الطف , وهو ما أشرف من أرض العرب على ريف العراق

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar recounts that his horse outpaced others until it nearly reached the Banū Zurayq mosque, illustrating something that rises close to a limit.
rows.anchor: كنت فارسا فسبقت الناس حتى طفت لي الفرس مسجد بني زريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quotes an unattributed saying that people are ‘sons of Adam, the measure’s slight shortfall’ as an example of ṭaff referring to a small amount.
rows.anchor: كلكم بنو آدم طف الصاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed roots are taking what is near at hand, as in an almost-full vessel; rationing; or reducing something petty. The author says the word suits fraud because the stolen amount is usually tiny.
rows.anchor: وكأنه اختير هذا اللفظ لأنه لا يكاد يسرق في الميزان والمكيال إلا الشيء اليسير جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā portrays the fraudsters as acting from a position of superiority over customers; they demand full or more than full measure for themselves.
rows.anchor: مستعلين أو متحاملين { على الناس } أي خاصة بمشاهدتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression may signal that they exploit anyone, especially a weak person; iktāl can take either min or ʿalā, while yastawfūn means they obtain complete measure eagerly and emphatically.
rows.anchor: وهذا الفعل يتعدى بمن وعلى , يقال : اكتال من الرجل وعليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits ‘weigh’ when describing their own purchases because weighing offers less opportunity for deliberate extra fullness than measuring; shortchanging, however, is possible in both.
rows.anchor: فكأنه ذكر ( اكتالوا ) ولم يذكر ( اتزنوا ) لأنه لا يتأتى في الوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When measuring or weighing for others, they reduce the amount owed; the object pronoun refers to customers’ due rights, and the wording foregrounds the recipient’s presence and the fraudsters’ habitual shamelessness.
rows.anchor: أي كالوا الناس أي حقهم أي ما لهم من الحق

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar treats kālūhum and wazanūhum as two words each, pausing after the verb and beginning with hum.
rows.anchor: وكان عيسى بن عمر يجعلهما حرفين يقف على كالوا ووزنوا ويبتدئ هم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbaydah prefers treating each verb and object pronoun as one written word, as supported by the codex spelling without an alif after the plural wāw.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : والاختيار الأولى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects taking hum as the object pronoun for the customers, arguing that it produces incoherent syntax and shifts the topic from the act to its agent.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون ضميرا للمطففين لأن الكلام يخرج به إلى نظم فاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author counters al-Zamakhsharī: the codex spelling supports the semantic reading that fraudsters take full or extra measure but give customers less.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن في خط المصحف تقوية لهذا الوجه المعنوي وتأكيدا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the warning to the record of every deed in 82:10 and the exact weighing of deeds in 21:47; fraud may seem small but is a major crime and merits a great warning.
rows.anchor: وإن عليكم لحافظين كراما كاتبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their habitual vice follows from feeling safe from punishment and denying the final accounting; the rhetorical question suggests even a mere suspicion of resurrection should restrain them, since decisive proofs have been given.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك لا يكون إلا ممن أمن العقاب وأنكر الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is a compelled awakening like rising from sleep, for the great day of gathering and accounting, when reward and punishment follow deeds; only God knows its full reality.
rows.anchor: بالبعث الذي قد ألفوا مثله من القهر باليقظة بعد القهر بالنوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanūd means intensely ungrateful and harsh in response to God, the benefactor who created, preserved, governed, and nurtured humanity; its intensive form describes one who scorns small favors and forgets many blessings over a little hardship.
rows.anchor: ومصدره الكنود بالضم وهو كفران النعمة

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ defines the ungrateful person as one bad experience making him forget many acts of kindness; gratitude is the opposite.
rows.anchor: هو من أنسته الخصلة الواحدة من الإساءةة الخصال الكثيرة من الإحسان

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads the oath as emphasizing humanity’s ingratitude and miserliness with wealth, as if no one would be held accountable for how it was acquired or spent; he cites 99:7–8.
rows.anchor: يبخل بما ليده من المال كأنه لا يجازي ولا يحاسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being is a witness against himself: under questioning he admits that all he has is God’s gift, that God forbade his disobedience, and that he has no right to act against his master’s will.
rows.anchor: لأنه مقر إذا حوقق بأن جميع ما هو فيه من إحسان ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khayr here means wealth; humanity loves it intensely and hoards it, preferring its immediate visible benefit over the delayed, unseen benefit of serving God.
rows.anchor: أي المال الذي لا يعد غيره لجهله خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah exposes the greatest losing faction, seduced by competing for abundance and destined for ruin on the Day of Calamity; the name al-Humazah signals its subject.
rows.anchor: مقصودها بيان الحزب الأكبر الخاسر الذي أهاه التكاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala presents God as sovereign and just, whose outward gifts reach both the miserly and generous, while His complete favor is reserved for whom He wills.
rows.anchor: الذي له تمام العز وهو الحكم العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamz originally means breaking and lamz piercing; both came to mean breaking people’s reputations and criticizing them. Ibn Hishām distinguishes public abuse and winking from secret faultfinding.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن هشام في تهذيب السيرة : الهمزة الذي يشتم الرجل علانية

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī says the intensified forms describe habitual mockery, whereas the passive forms with a still ending describe someone whom others mock; the author suggests the latter may deliberately make himself ridiculous.
rows.anchor: والفعلة بالسكون للمفعول وهو الذي يهمزه الناس ويلمزونه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the warning to 103:2: the collector imagines himself complete and faults others, while relying on wealth to preserve him; these are signs of human deficiency.
rows.anchor: رإن الإنسان لفي خسر } أتبعه بمثال من ذكر نقصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description singles out a wealthy person who needs no hoarding yet collects money, because people regard profit as success and boast of it; collecting wealth is the first sign of his loss.
rows.anchor: وكان المتمول عندهم هو الرابح , وهم يتفاخرون بالربح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read jamʿa with doubling, intensifying abundant collection; other reciters use the lighter form, while all double ʿaddada because the bare form can denote little.
rows.anchor: جاء التشديد في فعله لأبي جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collected wealth is substantial; he counts it until enumeration would take a long time, or stores and hoards it for future worldly needs.
rows.anchor: أي جعله بحيث إذا أريد عدده طال الزمان فيه وكثر التعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because of foolishness, he thinks his counted wealth makes him immortal in this world; alternatively, his immersion in sin and pleasure shows he acts as though he will never die, while only righteous deeds secure eternal life in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك كناية عن أنه عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects the fantasy: he will die like every other created living being.
rows.anchor: بل يموت كما مات كل حي مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After death he will certainly be flung into al-Ḥuṭamah, a layer of fire that crushes and breaks whatever enters it; the punishment answers his use of wealth to disregard others.
rows.anchor: أي الطبقة من النار التي من شأنها أن تحطم أي تكسر

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the names of Hell suit the form of punishment: Jahannam for confrontation and al-Ḥuṭamah for crushing retribution against hoarding.
rows.anchor: قال الأستاد أبو الحسن الحرالي : فلمعنى ما يختص بالحكم يسمى تعالى باسم من أسمائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question ‘What is al-Ḥuṭamah?’ magnifies a fire with no familiar worldly equivalent; it is called God’s fire to stress His majesty and punishment, and ‘kindled’ because He has ignited it.
rows.anchor: فإنه ليس في الوجود الذي شاهدتموه ما يقاربها ليكون مثالا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire reaches the hearts, the seat of belief and love of wealth from which corrupt convictions and deeds arise; the intelligent heart should have used its intelligence to seek deliverance.
rows.anchor: ولأنه منشأ العقائد الفاسدة ومعدن حب المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although heart exposure might seem to bring death and relief, the closed fire keeps its victims alive in unending torment; muʾṣadah means tightly shut upon them.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى خلودهم فيها وأنهم لا يموتون ولا ينقطع عنهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are confined in extended columns like a stockade with restraints, unable to move or escape; the structure reinforces the hopelessness already conveyed by the sealed fire.
rows.anchor: فهي في غاية المكنة فلا يستطيع الموثق بها على نوع حيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Fīl completes the warning of al-Humazah: those who rely on wealth, men, and mutual support are destroyed when their worldly means end, while complete power belongs to God alone; the title points to the army’s story.
rows.anchor: فعند انقطاعها أولى لأختصاصه سبحانه وتعالى بتمام القدرة دون التمكن بالمال والرجال

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains ‘he gathered wealth and counted it’ to mean that he counted or reckoned it; Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits the report.
rows.anchor: عن السدي في قوله : { جمع مالاً وعدده } قال : أحصاه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports that the Prophet recited yaḥsabu with kasrah on the sīn; Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Ḥākim authenticated this report, also cited by Ibn Mardawayh and al-Khaṭīb.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } بكسر السين

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrimah explains the claim that wealth made him immortal as meaning it increases his lifespan.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } قال : يزيد في عمره
